principles: Insurance is optional by general law unless a specific local rule says otherwise.
Ports, lenders, cargo owners, passenger services and contract issuers may independently require proof of coverage.
Policies contain operating restrictions. Violating one does not magically stop the ship; it creates financial and detection risk.
Insurers exchange enough records with reputable ports, registries, repair yards and claims investigators that undisclosed violations can be discovered.

certificate.name: Certificate of Insurance
certificate.verification: Reputable ports and contract issuers can validate certificates through commercial/registry data networks when connectivity permits.

requirements.typical: registration commonly required; insurance varies by system/berth
cargo and carrier-liability coverage commonly required
liability coverage commonly required by contract or port operator
liability and sometimes pollution/environmental coverage required
hull coverage normally required while lender retains financial interest
may require neither registration nor insurance

restrictions.example: Coverage valid through Lastlight but excludes travel beyond supported frontier.
No radioactive or high-hazard chemical cargo.
Named captain or appropriately licensed operator required.
Coverage applies only while vessel remains in registered/certified configuration.
Required inspections and maintenance intervals must remain current.

violation_model.description: A captain can knowingly operate outside policy terms. The insurer does not necessarily learn immediately.
detection_sources: cargo manifests supplied during contract verification
possible_outcomes: claim denial when violation is material to the loss
fraud investigation if the captain intentionally submitted false information
violation_model.gameplay_rule: Detection should be probabilistic where appropriate and strongly influenced by how visible the violating activity is. Filing a hazardous manifest at a major Concord terminal is far easier for an insurer to discover than an undocumented frontier trip from an informal dock.

market_effects: Insured operators gain access to higher-value contracts and reputable facilities.
Uninsured operation reduces fixed cost but shifts loss risk entirely to the captain.
Cheap policies can carry restrictive operating areas or high deductibles.
A cancelled policy can make replacement coverage more expensive.
Strong maintenance and claims history can improve rates over time.
